messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High p50/p95 latency and connection churn on /v1/chat/stream in prod-usw2 detected (alerts: streaming_latency_high, sse_conn_errors).

erin_oncall: got the page, looking now. can someone grab dashboards? :eyeglasses:

mike_eng-runtime: pulling traces — I see a spike in token generation time + a big tail in connection setup. 50% of requests stuck in `accept` for >300ms before first chunk.

jia_sre: also seeing a sustained rise in queued requests on gpu-pool-3. CPU of proxy nodes hit 95% during peaks. likely backpressure from runtime.

sam_support: Support is getting 3-4 tickets/min. customers reporting "stuck loading" in chat widgets. top affected tenants: acme-inc, teachio. No PII leaks noted.

erin_oncall: ok, need a live mitigation plan. options: 1) per-customer rate-limit bump down, 2) global ingress shaping for streaming routes, 3) temporarily pause streaming responses for chat and fall back to non-streaming generate. Thoughts?

mike_eng-runtime: pausing streaming for chat is the fastest and lowest-risk to reduce connection churn. We can flip a feature flag at the edge and return non-streaming chunked responses (single final response) for existing endpoints.

jia_sre: agree. rate limiting alone won't reduce connection count quickly enough. pausing streaming should cut active SSE connections and reduce pressure on proxies.

nina_product: product ok with temporary pause, want comms and clarity on expected behavior change for widgets.

erin_oncall: if we do this, we need to: 1) run `feature-toggle` to switch streaming->paused for prod-usw2; 2) add routing fallback so requests hit non-streaming handler; 3) update status page and support message template. mike, can you run the toggle? jia, can you add temporary ingress shaping rule if toggle doesn't land fast?

mike_eng-runtime: on it. running the toggle now.

-- command output --
mike_eng-runtime: ```
# uictl feature toggle
uictl set --env=prod --scope=region:us-west-2 streaming.push.enabled=false --reason "emergency egress churn"
Applying toggle to edge-config group: edge-prod-usw2
OK: feature applied to 48/48 edge nodes
``` 

deploy-bot: feature update: `streaming.push.enabled=false` applied to edge-prod-usw2 by mike_eng-runtime at 2026-03-15T15:12:34Z

mike_eng-runtime: toggled. pushing a small rollback guard in case we see regressions.

jia_sre: adding a temporary ingress cap to throttle new SSE connections at the LB layer (30 connections/s per customer) in case some clients retry aggressively.

-- command output --
jia_sre: ```
opsctl rate-limit add --service api-gateway --route "/v1/chat/stream" --limit 30/s --scope customer --env prod --region us-west-2
Response: rule created id=rl-usk-77
``` 

ops-bot: rate limit rule rl-usk-77 created (30/s per-customer) by jia_sre

sam_support: updating support macros now. Draft: "We've temporarily paused streaming chat responses in US-West-2 to improve latency. You will still receive full responses, but they may take slightly longer. We're working to restore streaming ASAP." Want to post to status page?

nina_product: yes, post to status page and push an in-app banner for affected tenants.

erin_oncall: good. monitoring: watch active SSE connections, p95 latency, and error rate. attendees: mike, jia, sam. I'll own incident until handoff.

-- 6 minutes later --

mike_eng-runtime: initial telemetry: active SSE connections down ~72%, p95 token latency dropped from 1.8s -> 700ms, proxy CPU normalized to 60%.

jia_sre: LB shows new connection attempts still, but most are handled by non-streaming handler now. error rate for 502 down to baseline.

sam_support: fewer new support tickets. customers on sendgrid-retry reported shorter load times.

erin_oncall: OK good progress. Let's keep the rules for 30 minutes and plan a gradual unpause after root cause triage. I've documented mitigation steps in the runbook.

mike_eng-runtime: note for root cause: kernel-level epoll backlog spikes when many clients keep SSE open and have long idle times; runtime garbage collection exacerbates when many KV caches warmed. investigating.

nina_product: I'd like a post-incident note to explain UX differences and timeline for restoring streaming.

erin_oncall: agreed. jia, please prepare rollback playbook: how to re-enable streaming and how to revoke ingress cap. mike, outline perf changes needed.

jia_sre: rollback commands ready:

-- snippet --
jia_sre: ```
uictl set --env=prod --scope=region:us-west-2 streaming.push.enabled=true --reason "rollback after validation"
opsctl rate-limit delete rl-usk-77 --env prod
``` 

deploy-bot: scheduled monitoring check at +10m and +30m.

-- 25 minutes after mitigation --

mike_eng-runtime: we've pushed a runtime patch candidate to reduce epoll backlog and adjust KV cache eviction thresholds. running canary in canary-usw2.

ops-bot: canary health: canary-usw2 stable for 8m. token p95 improved vs baseline.

erin_oncall: if canary is stable at +40m, we'll plan a gradual re-enable of streaming on 10% of edge nodes and monitor.

sam_support: drafting public update: "Incident: Streaming responses paused in US-West-2 to stabilize latency. Most customers will see full responses via non-streaming endpoints. We expect partial re-enable within 90 minutes pending validation." Will coordinate with ops.

erin_oncall: handing off to jia_sre for monitoring and re-enable steps. I'll update incident channel when I resume oncall at next shift.

jia_sre: taking over monitoring and rollback timeline. I'll post updates every 10m.

mike_eng-runtime: leaving notes in the incident doc about runtime adjustments and next steps for a more permanent mitigation (prefetch connection drop handling, adaptive keepalive).

sam_support: will update affected customers and close incoming tickets with the macro.

erin_oncall: thanks team. :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigation in place, impact reduced. assignee -> jia_sre. severity -> S2. thread archived to incidents.
